chunks: As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: Some people have related that this is the saying of the Messenger of Allāh, peace be upon him and his descendants.

key_terms.السَّيِّدُ الرِّضْيُ: As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī, a prominent Shia scholar and compiler of Nahj al-Balagha
key_terms.النَّبِيِّ: The Prophet, referring to Muhammad (peace be upon him)
key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his family, a common honorific for the Prophet

ai.seo_question: Who attributed this saying to the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi attributes this maxim on contentment to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), thereby elevating it from a general wisdom saying to a definitive prophetic tradition (hadith). This attribution underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Prophet’s role as the primary source of ethical guidance, linking the spiritual wealth of satisfaction directly to divine revelation.
